how: The starter calls members to help build the logo and supplies a concrete design.
The same member proposes the logo and lays out the dots and border for others to build.
Starting and calling for help occur in the same member's opening contributions rather than as separately demonstrated stages.
A proposed logo and specified dots and border instantiate design selection without showing collective argument over the design.
A member reports trying to build and the organiser later reports that the group completed the logo.
The call is followed by a member reporting an attempt to build, without establishing that the call caused that member to start.
A changed plan directs readers to a linked new location for the logo.
Instructions and a later changed plan do not show an argument settled by a posted agreed template.
A brief thanks accepts the reported relocation discussion and asks for nothing back.
Joining can include a complaint, while bare thanks answers a later relocation proposal rather than demonstrating an obligation created by the placement call.
Visitors report running scripts for their flag, which creates an automated constraint on the logo's location.
Treat seeking bot assistance as preparation until deployment is evidenced, because the exchange ends with grid work rather than confirmed automated rebuilding.
Practical instructions and contact with another room's moderators cannot test a cross-room frequency claim or exclude decisions made outside this record.
A late start and script pressure do not establish a spoken judgment that the room has too few hands.
A report that the logo is overrun is followed by a visitor reporting defence against persistent old scripts.
Reported completion precedes contested defence, supporting the sequence without identifying every cause of damage.
Visitors explain overwriting through flag scripts and sleeping users rather than attributing every changed pixel to deliberate hostility.
The organiser proposes and sends a truce to neighbouring box builders.
The organiser contacts Quebec to ask that expanding flags spare the logo.
Participants negotiate possible new sites and report an ongoing deal for space above HEYYEA.
The organiser carries a message to another room and reports replying there directly.
Cross-language negotiation includes seeking a French speaker, receiving a reasoned refusal, and substituting machine translation.
Explanations and corrections about neighbouring flags support understanding while participants seek an agreement.
The organiser reports an alliance expected to watch the logo, establishing a claimed bilateral tie without verifying reciprocal defence.
The reported alliance does not establish that a shared threat caused its formation.
The request for Quebec to leave the dots alone explicitly responds to threatened flag expansion.
Negotiation can begin during building and continue alongside defence rather than requiring a separate completed upkeep stage first.
Participants announce a changed location and later propose alternative sites while negotiating where to rebuild.
Admit negotiated or anticipatory relocation under persistent scripts without requiring an explicit fight-versus-move deliberation, and leave the final move unresolved.
The visitor explicitly links relocation to flag scripts, while the proposed lack-of-hands cause remains unobserved.
A neighbour answers the proposed site by promising not to touch outside its own logo and apologising.
A verbal boundary commitment does not establish realised restraint while old scripts continue overwriting the protected work.
Realising promised restraint requires reaching the sleeping users whose old scripts continue changing the logo.
Old scripts and requests for moderator contact do not show anyone disputing who may bind the room to an agreement.
Negotiation and continued overwriting do not establish that a dispute over representation followed the agreement.
The organiser asks neighbours for bot rebuilding help and receives a conditional offer alongside an explanation of limited capacity.
Strain leads to seeking and conditionally arranging help here, but neither delivery nor sufficient spare capacity is established.
The boundary assurance is answered by a rebuild request, showing the negotiation channel being used to seek assistance.
Bot assistance depends on usable images, a location, moderator contact, and account capacity not already committed to the helper's own work.
Rebuilding assistance requires agreeing image specifications and preparing a grid before a visitor can complete the remaining preparation.
An ongoing relocation deal answers a defence report, making moving and holding the current mark concurrent activities.
Moderator contact for bot help and a pending location deal cannot establish a completed host-governed guest arrangement.
Visiting speakers explain and correct the national history of the neighbouring flags within the negotiation.
Attribute historical explanations to their visiting speakers rather than inferring that the host room adopted their national identity or political motive.
Visitors explaining the flags do not establish a quarrel that the host room carried in from before the canvas.
Historical explanations and a hope for agreement cannot test the cross-room claim linking prior ties to calls for attack.
Enthusiastic instructions for a logo do not establish host-subreddit April Fools keying.
The supplied placement call does not establish containment of canvas talk or demonstrate that containment was unnecessary.
The placement call supplies no evidence of a flood causing host moderation or boundary rules.
An arrival celebrates completion and another visitor praises the discovered logo.
Celebration and confirmation of completion are directly joined in the exchange rather than separated into successive stages.
The overrun report records the logo's immediate fate during active work rather than preserving a final retrospective.
Celebration precedes a damage report, but the record supports that sequence without showing that celebrating caused record preservation.
The last coded report concerns a pending new building site and leaves post-event continuation unobserved.
A damage report and ongoing relocation negotiations do not show recording leading to a lasting project.
Correcting flag history during negotiation and seeking a new site cannot test post-placement disputes over the preserved canvas.
Neighbours' expansion and scripts do not establish that members of the host room organised an attack.
The recruitment call is followed by building and truce proposals without supplying evidence that the room called for an attack.
A complaint about square builders and an overrun report do not establish an ongoing verbal contest with a rival.
Protective negotiations without a visible attack call cannot test the proposed consequences of the room initiating an attack.
